content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 (no action): both queues are predicted to stay above the 80% target from 15:30 to 20:00 at no extra cost.","why":"The absences (19 on payments, 10 on general) are mostly bus-strike lateness rather than illness, and payments volume is 12% below forecast, so the gap is partly offset. With no changes, service level over 15:30-20:00 is predicted at 87.8% (payments 84.3%, general 92.3%) with 2.9% abandons. That clears the 80% target, so no paid action is needed.","trade_offs":["P1 (no-cost rebalance) costs nothing either, but it lowers payments to 81.8% and overall to 87.1% while lifting general to 94.2%. It adds break delays and agent moves for a slightly worse result.","P4 (₹348) raises payments to 87.7% and overall to 90.8%, with abandons down to 2.1%. It is the cheapest real improvement if you want more margin on payments.","P2 (₹2,160) and P3 (₹3,672) give the strongest service: 92.3% and 94.1% overall, with abandons of 1.8% and 1.3%. That is meaningful extra spend when the target is already met.","Payments at 84.3% has the thinnest margin under P0, about 4 points above target."],"watch":"Watch general handle time, which has run 15% above forecast for the last two intervals, and payments service level against the 80% line. If late agents don't arrive as expected or payments drifts toward 80%, switch to P4 as a low-cost fallback."}
